recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is required for FHIR-20627 unless a future Patient Care decision wants editorial rewording of the occurrence[x] definition text; the conformance surface and search parameter already expose Timing.
issue_request: FHIR-20627 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification for the STU3 request that Procedure.occurrence support Timing, specifically for recurring historical or ongoing procedures such as physical therapy or counseling twice weekly. The resolution requested renaming Procedure.performed to Procedure.occurrence, adding Procedure.occurrenceTiming, and removing the procedure-schedule extension.
initial_application: Jira points to merge commit 88c604c66b028201ee797438b5154f3366ee7ec0. That PR summary explicitly included GF#20627, and the first-parent diff changed Procedure.performed[x] to Procedure.occurrence[x], added GF#20627 to the occurrence row, and added Timing to the historical Procedure spreadsheet source. Later source refactoring preserved the result in source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml.
additional_context: Procedure is active in source/fhir.ini. source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml defines Procedure.occurrence[x] with committee note GF#13246, GF#20627 and includes Timing as an allowed type. source/fhir.ini maps Procedure.performed[x] to Procedure.occurrence[x], and source/procedure/bundle-Procedure-search-params.xml includes Procedure.occurrence.ofType(Timing) in the Procedure-date expression. The procedure-schedule definition is absent from core and exists only in the FHIR Extension Pack as version-specific historical support ending at FHIR 4.3 with guidance to use Procedure.occurrenceTiming in R5+.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the build-scope core conformance source already supports Timing on Procedure.occurrence[x], preserves the old performed[x] path as a migration alias, and does not carry an active core procedure-schedule extension.

related_jiras.note: A separate published FHIR-I review of choice-type search parameters surfaced during Jira search; current Procedure-date already includes Timing, but that broader issue was not decided here.
